ref_extractions.title: Building FAIR Functionality: Annotating Events in Time Series Data Using Hierarchical Event Descriptors (HED)
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper describes the HED-3G framework and tools for event annotation in electrophysiological data. It discusses HED schema development and annotation best practices but does not use any specific EEG dataset for analysis.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: General HED framework paper; no dataset-specific analysis presented

ref_extractions.title: A multi-subject, multi-modal human neuroimaging dataset
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This is the original publication describing the Wakeman and Henson face processing MEEG dataset from 2015. It describes the paradigm and experimental design that the HED-annotated version (ds003645) replicates, but it describes the original openfmri dataset (ds000117), not the HED-annotated OpenNeuro version.
ref_extractions.super_meta_note: Original 2015 paper; dataset described is ds000117/openfmri, not the HED-annotated ds003645
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Describes original face processing MEEG dataset with famous/unfamiliar/scrambled conditions; paradigm replicated in ds003645 but this paper describes the original version

ref_extractions.title: FastSurfer - A fast and accurate deep learning based neuroimaging pipeline
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper describes FastSurfer, a deep learning pipeline for structural MRI brain segmentation and cortical thickness analysis. It focuses on volumetric analysis of T1-weighted MRI scans, entirely unrelated to EEG/MEG face processing data.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Structural MRI deep learning paper; no EEG/MEG data used

ref_extractions.title: Capturing the nature of events and event context using hierarchical event descriptors (HED)
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper explicitly uses the HED-annotated Wakeman and Henson dataset from OpenNeuro (ds003645) as a case study. The authors made available an HED-annotated BIDS-formatted edition of the MEEG data at openneuro.org/ds003645 and demonstrate face type classification as the ML task using the three stimulus conditions.
ref_extractions.super_meta_note: HED-annotated version (ds003645) explicitly used; demonstrates super-level metadata annotation
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Uses ds003645 specifically; compares famous/unfamiliar/scrambled face conditions with HED event annotations

ref_extractions.title: EEG is better left alone
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper evaluates automated EEG preprocessing methods using percentage of significant channels as a quality metric. While it uses a Face dataset with familiar vs scrambled faces, the analysis focuses on preprocessing pipeline comparison (filtering, referencing, artifact rejection) rather than using the dataset for a defined ML classification task.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Uses face symmetry judgment task data to compare preprocessing pipelines; not used for ML classification

ref_extractions.title: A multi-subject, multi-modal human neuroimaging dataset
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: Duplicate reference to the 2015 Wakeman and Henson original dataset paper. Describes the same paradigm that ds003645 replicates but refers to the original openfmri version, not the HED-annotated OpenNeuro edition.
ref_extractions.super_meta_note: Original dataset paper; ds003645 is HED-annotated version of this paradigm
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Original Wakeman and Henson 2015 publication; dataset precursor to ds003645

ref_extractions.title: MEG-BIDS, the brain imaging data structure extended to magnetoencephalography
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper describes the MEG-BIDS specification for standardizing MEG data organization. While it mentions the Wakeman and Henson dataset in passing and BIDS supports HED annotations, the paper focuses on data format standards, not analysis of this specific dataset.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: MEG-BIDS specification paper; dataset mentioned as example but not analyzed

ref_extractions.title: Multimodal Integration of M/EEG and fMRI Data in SPM12
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper uses the Wakeman and Henson face processing dataset for a SPM12 tutorial on multimodal integration. However, it uses OpenNeuro dataset ds000117 (BIDS version of original), not the HED-annotated ds003645. The paradigm is the same but the dataset version differs.
ref_extractions.super_meta_note: Uses ds000117, not ds003645; similar paradigm but different dataset version
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Tutorial paper using Wakeman/Henson data at ds000117 version

ref_extractions.title: Capturing the nature of events and event context using hierarchical event descriptors (HED)
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: Duplicate entry of the HED paper from NeuroImage 2021. This version from Europe PMC contains the same content and explicitly uses ds003645 (HED-annotated Wakeman and Henson dataset) as a case study for event annotation, demonstrating face type classification with the three stimulus conditions.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Same paper as NeuroImage 2021; uses ds003645 for HED annotation demonstration

tasks_section:
## Tasks

### Classical Task 1: Face Type Classification (Famous vs Unfamiliar vs Scrambled)
- **Task Type**: classification
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_event_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: tmin = -0.5 s, tmax = 1.2 s, target_events = [`trial_type` from events.tsv]
- **Label Route**: `event`
- **Meta Level**: raw
- **Target Definition**:
  | Event | y | Meaning |
  |-------|---|---------|
  | famous | 0 | Famous/familiar face stimulus |
  | unfamiliar | 1 | Unfamiliar/non-famous face stimulus |
  | scrambled | 2 | Scrambled face stimulus (control) |
- **Evidence**:
  - DOI: 10.1016/j.neuroimage.2021.118766 — Capturing the nature of events and event context using HED; uses ds003645 for three-class face perception classification (famous/familiar vs unfamiliar vs scrambled), demonstrates HED annotation schema mapping for face stimulus events.
- **Kernel Notes**: Parse events.tsv `trial_type` column for face category labels. Expected values: 'famous'/'Famous_Familiar' (class 0), 'unfamiliar'/'Unfamiliar' (class 1), 'scrambled'/'Scrambled' (class 2). Verify exact spelling from dataset sidecar. High-count numerical event IDs (event_1–event_9 with ~120,000 counts) are MEG/EEG system status markers—exclude from epoching. Focus on lower-count events (~200–2000 per type) for stimulus-locked analysis. Isolate EEG channels from 395-channel MEEG set before processing.
